title: Potential Energy
body:
**Potential energy** is energy stored by an object's position in a field or by the
configuration of a system. Two forms appear in this course.

```
gravitational (near the surface):   U = mgh
a spring:                           U = ½kx²
```

The height $h$ is measured from a reference level the solver chooses, which makes the absolute
value arbitrary and the change in it meaningful. Choosing the reference at the lowest point of
the motion is what keeps the arithmetic simple.

Potential energy exists only for a conservative force, one whose [[Work]] depends on the start
and end points and not on the path between them. Gravity and an ideal spring qualify, and
[[Friction]] does not, which is why there is no friction potential energy and why its losses
have to be tracked separately.

[[Conservation of Energy]] is what the concept exists for: the sum of potential and
[[Kinetic Energy]] stays constant while only conservative forces act, so a problem is
solved by evaluating the total at two moments. [[MATHEMATICAL METHODS]] generalises the
condition, where a conservative force is a [[Conservative Vector Field]] and the
potential energy is the scalar field it is the gradient of.
